Take line along latitude 60 longitude 0 longitude 100. planar middle line (50, 60). great circle middle long way north : thousand kilometres. Neither answer wrong, two different shapes happen share vertices. matters knowing one data means. s2 makes geodesic reading default; bigcurve assumes . bigcurve inserts new vertices exactly s2’s arc. Densify line ask s2 far new vertex line: nanometres, floating point noise. added vertices change nothing shape sphere; make explicit flat drawing.
code: line <- s2_make_line(c(0, 100), c(60, 60)) s2_as_text(s2_interpolate_normalized(line, 0.5)) #> [1] "POINT (49.99999999999999 69.63942512488693)"  ## how far is the planar middle from the true line, in metres? s2_distance(s2_lnglat(50, 60), line) #> [1] 1071857 d <- densify(segment(c(0, 100), c(60, 60)),              "+proj=laea +lon_0=50 +lat_0=60", tolerance = 1000) nrow(d) #> [1] 13 max(s2_distance(s2_lnglat(d[, 1], d[, 2]), line)) #> [1] 1.749256e-09

code: box <- s2_make_polygon(c(100, 160, 160, 100), c(-35, -35, -20, -20)) south <- s2_make_line(c(100, 160), c(-35, -35)) s2_as_text(s2_interpolate_normalized(south, 0.5)) #> [1] "POINT (130 -38.95657940063204)" prj <- "+proj=laea +lon_0=130 +lat_0=-30" pool <- wkpool::establish_topology(wk::as_wkb(box)) dense <- densify(pool, prj) ## the planar reading: sides that follow parallels and meridians lon <- seq(100, 160, by = 0.5) planar <- rbind(cbind(lon, -35), cbind(160, seq(-35, -20, by = 0.5)),                 cbind(rev(lon), -20), cbind(100, seq(-20, -35, by = -0.5))) ## back to geometry, then project with wk and PROJ ## (merge_coincident() closes the ring where its last vertex repeats the first) geom <- wkpool::cycles_to_wkb(wkpool::merge_coincident(dense)) to_map <- PROJ::proj_trans_create(wk::wk_crs(geom), prj) drawn <- wk::wk_transform(geom, to_map) flat <- wk::wk_transform(wk::xy(planar[, 1], planar[, 2], crs = "OGC:CRS84"), to_map)  fc <- wk::wk_coords(flat) dc <- wk::wk_coords(drawn) op <- par(mar = rep(0.5, 4)) plot(range(fc$x, dc$x), range(fc$y, dc$y), type = "n", asp = 1,      axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "") lines(fc$x, fc$y, col = "grey60", lwd = 3) plot(drawn, lwd = 1.5, add = TRUE) points(dc$x, dc$y, pch = 19, cex = 0.4) par(op)

code: lon <- seq(-180, 150, by = 30) lat <- seq(-75, -45, by = 15) cells <- expand.grid(x = lon, y = lat) wkt <- sprintf("POLYGON ((%s %s, %s %s, %s %s, %s %s, %s %s))",                cells$x, cells$y, cells$x + 30, cells$y, cells$x + 30, cells$y + 15,                cells$x, cells$y + 15, cells$x, cells$y) pool <- wkpool::establish_topology(wk::wkt(wkt, crs = "OGC:CRS84"))  prj <- "+proj=laea +lon_0=0 +lat_0=-90" out <- densify(pool, prj) c(input = nrow(wkpool::pool_vertices(pool)),   densified = nrow(wkpool::pool_vertices(out))) #>     input densified  #>       180       360 merged_after <- wkpool::pool_vertices(wkpool::merge_coincident(out)) merged_first <- wkpool::pool_vertices(densify(wkpool::merge_coincident(pool), prj)) nrow(merged_after) #> [1] 184 identical(sort(complex(real = merged_after$x, imaginary = merged_after$y)),           sort(complex(real = merged_first$x, imaginary = merged_first$y))) #> [1] TRUE geom <- wkpool::cycles_to_wkb(wkpool::merge_coincident(out)) drawn <- wk::wk_transform(geom, PROJ::proj_trans_create(wk::wk_crs(geom), prj)) xy <- wk::wk_coords(drawn) op <- par(mar = rep(0.5, 4)) plot(range(xy$x), range(xy$y), type = "n", asp = 1, axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "") plot(drawn, add = TRUE, col = "grey95") points(xy$x, xy$y, pch = 19, cex = 0.3) par(op)

title: bigcurve 0.6.0
text: First CRAN release. Edges shared neighbouring polygons now refine identical vertices. refinement arithmetic always runs one canonical direction chain reversed afterwards, -> b b -> give bitwise identical new vertices (previously differed last bits, wkpool::merge_coincident() fuse ). edge occurs vertices (merged pool, segment mesh) refined new vertices reused. densify() now really defaults source = NULL, wkpool input’s crs used. Previously documented default one code, pool projected units read degrees. default tolerance now derived larger side projected extent, single parallel meridian (zero width one direction) longer errors. Requires wkpool >= 0.4.0 (CRAN) pool input; fallbacks older wkpool versions, vctrs utils dependencies needed, gone. glue longer used. New vignette, “bigcurve s2”, contrasting bigcurve s2. Credit licence notice d3-geo resampling method inst/COPYRIGHTS; Mike Bostock added contributor copyright holder.

title: bigcurve 0.1.0
text: New header-C++ core R PROJ dependency, driving refinement target-plane metric: perpendicular distance projected great circle midpoint planar chord, parametric shear check, forced split arcs wider 30 degrees, maximum depth. point transformed exactly inverse transforms used, refinement dramatically faster 0.0.x loop.
